definition: OpenCode is a free and open-source artificial intelligence coding agent developed by Anomaly.
details: It connects large language models with software projects and development tools, allowing users to inspect, modify, optimize source code, run script commands, tests, and perform other programming tasks through natural-language instructions. OpenCode can be used through a terminal, desktop application, or integrated development environment (IDE), and supports models from more than 75 providers, including Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, as well as locally hosted models.

explainer.lead: OpenCode is a free and open-source AI coding agent developed by Anomaly that connects large language models to software projects and development tools. It matters because it lets developers inspect, modify and test code through natural-language instructions.

tiers.eli5: It is a coding helper you can talk to: you describe what you want, and it changes your project's code and runs the tests.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can use it from a terminal, desktop app or IDE, and can point it at models from more than 75 providers, including Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, or locally hosted models. The pitfall is the usual one for coding agents: broad model choice does not remove the need to review what it changes.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source coding agent from Anomaly that links LLMs to projects and tooling for source inspection, modification, optimization and running commands and tests. It supports over 75 model providers plus local models.

explainer.example: A developer can ask OpenCode in the terminal to modify source code and run the test suite, using a model from any of its supported providers or a local one.
